headline: Etsy marketplace GMS rose 5.5% (3.6% FX-neutral) and buyers grew again quarter over quarter; FY GMS outlook raised to low single digits.
guidance_note: FY 2026 marketplace GMS growth raised to low single digits (from slight growth); Q2 GMS guided to $2.48-2.53bn (+3-5%); FY adj. EBITDA margin 28-30% unchanged.
key_messages: Etsy marketplace GMS ~$2.46bn, +5.5% YoY but only +3.6% FX-neutral; management cited FX and an easy prior-year comparison.
Active buyers 86.6m (TTM), the first quarter-over-quarter gain in two years; GMS per active buyer $122 (TTM).
App GMS +11.2% YoY (vs 6.6% in Q4), about 47% of GMS; active sellers +3.3% to 5.6m.
CEO says listing-price increases after de minimis ended and tariffs began are likely 'sticky'; Etsy will lap that boost later.
Depop to be sold to eBay ($1.2bn at the time); $145m of stock bought back.

consumer.big_ticket: Discretionary GMS growth was modest ex-FX and helped by higher prices; management said gains in buyer frequency and retention will take time.
consumer.pricing: Listing prices rose after the de minimis exemption ended and tariffs began; CEO expects those increases to stick.
consumer.quote: Those increases are probably sticky price increases (CEO Kruti Patel Goyal on tariff and de minimis-related listing prices).

macro_read: Q1 2026 growth at a discretionary marketplace came largely from higher prices and FX rather than volume, which fits a consumer still spending but absorbing tariff-driven price increases.
notes: Continuing-operations consolidated GMS fell 3.9% because the prior year included Reverb.

Etsy reports GAAP only; the EPS shown is GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations ($0.89; continuing net income $104.7m vs a $35.1m loss a year earlier, which included a $101.7m impairment). One transcript summary cited $0.60 on an unstated basis.
Depop is in discontinued operations; Reverb (sold mid-2025) is in the prior-year continuing base, so consolidated GMS fell 3.9% while marketplace GMS rose 5.5%.
FX lifted reported marketplace GMS growth by about 1.9 pts (5.5% reported vs 3.6% FX-neutral).
Revenue consensus ($621.1m) comes from a single source (Investing.com).
Stock reaction left null: only low-quality aggregators (+1.7% / +2.7%) found.
